item.subject: maths
item.stem:
The figure shows Esha's $5$-by-$5$ square of unit tiles. She paints it in nested L-shaped borders: the outermost border uses $9$ tiles, the next uses $7$, then $5$, then $3$, and the centre tile is $1$.

Why does the sum of the first $5$ odd numbers equal $5^{2}$?

options.A: The $5$-by-$5$ square partitions into those five nested odd L-borders, so $1+3+5+7+9=25$.
options.B: Any set of odd numbers sums to a square, even when the odds are not the first five consecutive odds from $1$.
options.C: The same L-border story also forces the sum of the first five counting numbers to equal $25$.
options.D: The answer is $25$, because $5$ is the largest number printed on the figure.
